title: AI scams in Georgia and South Florida: How scammers use deepfakes to steal millions

reading.body:
Criminals are using generative AI to create voice clones and deepfakes of real people, including a South Florida immigration attorney, to impersonate them in fraud schemes. The scams target vulnerable populations such as immigrants seeking legal services and victims of romance and investment fraud. The technology makes these traditional scams harder to detect because the impersonations are more convincing than earlier fraud attempts.

The deployment failure here is that generative AI systems capable of creating voice clones and realistic synthetic media lack adequate safeguards against misuse. These systems were built and released into general use without sufficient controls to prevent their application in impersonation and fraud. Detecting this would have required either restricting access to such systems, implementing authentication mechanisms, or conducting threat modeling on how criminals might weaponize voice and video synthesis.

Whether the developers of these AI systems were aware of the risks, negligent in preventing misuse, or deliberately indifferent is not established by these reports. The scams are confirmed through law enforcement complaints and financial losses documented in the FBI's 2025 Internet Crime Report.

summary:
Scammers are increasingly using artificial intelligence technology to create convincing deepfakes and voice clones to defraud victims. A South Florida immigration attorney discovered criminals had cloned his voice to target immigrants, while a Cobb County couple in metro Atlanta lost approximately 800,000 dollars in a cryptocurrency scam. According to the FBI's 2025 Internet Crime Report, Americans reported nearly 893 million dollars in losses from AI-enabled scams last year, with the technology making traditional frauds like romance schemes and fake investment opportunities harder to detect.

Florida and Georgia have been particularly affected, with Florida reporting 350 AI-related complaints totaling nearly 39.9 million dollars in losses and Georgia reporting 71 complaints with over 10.4 million dollars in losses. Criminals use generative AI to clone voices from social media, spoof phone numbers, create fake photos, and research family relationships to make scams more believable. To protect themselves, consumers should establish code words with loved ones, verify urgent requests by contacting people directly, never send money based solely on phone calls, and report suspected scams to law enforcement and the FBI.
